title: Retirement leaves non-terminal git-history activation journals that redrive forever
wanted_capability: The retirement journal should discharge (supersede or remove) the retired project's typed git-history activation journals and their source generations. Today retirement discharges catalog rows, index refs, vectors, and coordination rows, then the producer grant is revoked, but every non-terminal HistoryActivationStageV1 journal under git-sources/repos/<repo_history>/history/ survives. The activation worker enumerates non-terminal journals on every redrive tick, each one fails with repo_history_not_found (no transport grant for a retired repo), and the daemon logs one warning per journal every ~30 seconds indefinitely. Six such journals from the last retirement batch are still redriving. Wanted: a discharge stage that marks those journals Superseded (terminal) or deletes them, mirroring the locality-marker discharge gap in the same family.
missing_primitive: a git-history activation-journal discharge stage in the retirement journal, or a redrive policy that terminates journals whose repo history has no grant and no catalog member
fallback_used: None applied; the warnings are noise only. A manual cleanup would be a maintenance-pod removal of the journal files with the daemon stopped.
evidence: sibling gap-7e4c11ce (retirement does not discharge locality marker rows)
src/server/history_activation.rs spawn_worker: pending set is refilled from list_activation_journals() filtered on !stage.terminal()
